moduleName: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments

questions.questionText: Why is SMS-based Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) considered less secure than authenticator apps?

options.text: SMS text messages cost money to receive.
SMS messages can be intercepted via SIM-swapping, smishing, or cellular network exploitation.
Authenticator apps require an active satellite connection.
SMS codes only work on desktop computers.

questions.explanation: SMS relies on vulnerable cellular protocols subject to interception and SIM swaps.

questions.questionText: Connecting a remote work laptop to an isolated "Guest Network" on your home router helps protect work data from compromised smart home IoT devices.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Guest networks isolate work devices from unpatched IoT appliances on the main subnet.

questions.questionText: You accidentally enter your work password on a suspicious website landing page. What is the FIRST technical action you should take?

options.text: Restart your home router.
Immediately disconnect your computer from Wi-Fi/Ethernet and report the incident to security/IT to reset credentials.
Wait 48 hours to see if someone logs in.
Delete your web browser icon.

questions.explanation: Disconnecting limits malware/session exfiltration, and immediate reporting allows rapid password/session revocation.

questions.questionText: What is the risk of keeping factory default administrative credentials on your home Wi-Fi router?

options.text: It reduces internet download speed by 50%.
Default credentials are publicly known, allowing attackers to compromise the router and intercept traffic.
Routers automatically turn off after 24 hours if defaults are kept.
It prevents mobile phones from connecting.

questions.explanation: Botnets and attackers target default router passwords to gain network control.

questions.questionText: Which of the following authentication methods provide resistance against phishing attacks? *(Select TWO)*

options.text: Plain text passwords sent via email.
FIDO2 / WebAuthn Hardware Security Keys (e.g., YubiKey).
App-based Time-based One-Time Passwords (TOTP).
Standard SMS text passcodes.

questions.explanation: FIDO2 keys and TOTP authenticator apps are significantly more secure than plain passwords or SMS.

questions.questionText: Postponing operating system security updates for several months improves laptop battery performance and network security.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Unpatched operating systems leave known security vulnerabilities exposed to software exploits.

questions.questionText: A client emails asking you to wire project funds to a new bank account. The email comes from the client's real address. What is the safest out-of-band verification step?

options.text: Reply to the email asking: *"Is this account really yours?"*
Call the client on a phone number verified from your original signed contract to confirm the change verbally.
Wire half the money first to test the account.
Send the money via cryptocurrency instead.

questions.explanation: Always verify banking detail changes via an independent, trusted communication channel.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of a Password Manager for remote workers?

options.text: To share passwords publicly with friends.
To generate and securely store unique, complex passwords for every account, mitigating credential stuffing risks.
To automatically bypass MFA prompts.
To speed up Wi-Fi processing.

questions.explanation: Password managers eliminate password reuse across multiple corporate and personal sites.

questions.questionText: Using the same password across both personal personal banking and corporate work portals is acceptable as long as the password contains at least 8 letters.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Password reuse enables credential stuffing: if one site is breached, attackers try the credentials across all accounts.

questions.questionText: Which wireless encryption standard provides the strongest security for home Wi-Fi networks?

options.text: WEP (Wired Equivalent Privacy)
WPA3 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 3)
Plain HTTP
WPA1

questions.explanation: WPA3 is the current state-of-the-art Wi-Fi encryption standard.

questions.questionText: You are working remotely from a coffee shop. What tool should you use to encrypt your internet traffic before connecting to the open public Wi-Fi?

options.text: Public BitTorrent client
Virtual Private Network (VPN) or encrypted tunnel
Incognito browser tab
Adobe Acrobat Reader

questions.explanation: VPNs create an encrypted tunnel that protects data from eavesdropping on unencrypted public Wi-Fi networks.

questions.questionText: What should you do with unused smart home devices connected to your primary work Wi-Fi network?

options.text: Move them to an isolated Guest Network or update/disable unused connectivity.
Share their IP addresses on social media.
Connect them directly to your work laptop via USB.
Turn off your laptop firewall.

questions.explanation: Isolating or hardening smart devices prevents them from serving as entry points to work machines.

questions.questionText: An incognito or private browsing window completely protects your computer from downloading malware.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Incognito mode prevents local browser history storage; it does not block malware downloads or network attacks.

questions.questionText: Which actions are part of solid remote work cyber hygiene? *(Select TWO)*

options.text: Reusing the same master password for all work accounts.
Applying automatic software and security updates on all endpoints.
Securing home Wi-Fi networks with strong passwords and WPA2/WPA3 encryption.
Disabling Multi-Factor Authentication to speed up login times.

questions.explanation: Regular software patching and Wi-Fi encryption are fundamental security practices.

questions.questionText: You notice a USB flash drive sitting on your home office desk. You do not remember buying it or where it came from. What should you do?

options.text: Plug it into your work laptop to see what files are on it.
Do not plug it into your laptop; report untrusted media to IT or safely dispose of it.
Give it to a neighbor to test on their computer.
Format it while holding it in your hands.

questions.explanation: Unknown USB drives (baiting) can execute hardware-level keystroke injection or malware scripts.

questions.questionText: Reporting a security mistake immediately to your IT team is better than hiding it, because swift response minimizes organizational damage.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Early reporting allows security teams to revoke compromised tokens before lateral movement occurs.

questions.questionText: What feature in web browsers helps protect users from accessing known malicious websites?

options.text: Auto-play video settings
Built-in Phishing and Malware Protection (e.g., Safe Browsing filters)
Custom font downloads
Cookie clear timers

questions.explanation: Browser reputation filters warn users before navigating to flagged phishing or malware domains.

questions.questionText: What is the safest way to store physical backup codes for your account MFA?

options.text: Stick them on a Post-it note attached to your computer monitor.
Store them in a secure location, such as an encrypted password manager or secure physical safe.
Post them on a public web page.
Email them to an unknown address.

questions.explanation: MFA backup codes grant full account recovery access and must be protected like primary passwords.

questions.questionText: Which steps should be taken when setting up a personal BYOD smartphone for remote work access? *(Select TWO)*

options.text: Enable device PIN/Biometric lock screen settings.
Disable automatic operating system security updates.
Install authorized mobile security software or MDM profiles as required by policy.
Root or jailbreak the phone to remove all manufacturer security restrictions.

questions.explanation: Lock screen controls and security software prevent physical and unauthorized software access.

questions.questionText: In a remote work environment, cybersecurity is solely the responsibility of corporate IT staff, and individual employees play no role in defense.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Without traditional enterprise perimeters, individual remote workers serve as the primary line of defense against social engineering attacks.
